D_8006D350_6DF50.summary: Unsigned 16-bit allocation limits indexed by native pool kind.
behavior: The chain allocator subtracts active counts from this table to decide whether a request fits. Element 2 controls model/display records.

Changing a numeric limit does not create backing records or expand related actor-owner capacity. Engine initialization can restore the table; any capacity customization must account for the complete pool lifecycle.

func_08001020_6F4500.title: Update a live locked doorway
func_08001020_6F4500.summary: Updates native doorway interaction and padlock-removal state.
behavior: The door stores its lock flag at +0xD4, interaction latch at +0xDA and state word at +0xEC. State bit 0x1 requests unlocking, 0x2 marks unlocked completion and 0x4 belongs to interaction state.

After key/save accounting is complete, an active padlock can be asked to run its native disappearance by clearing the interaction latch/bit and setting the unlocking bit. Keep the original parent callback so child completion and normal doorway interaction retain their native flow.
cautions: The lock save bit and key accounting must already be applied exactly once before the live animation.
Leave the parent callback intact so the update does not pull the local player through the doorway.

func_08007D24_6BAFC4.title: Congo native victory callback
func_08007D24_6BAFC4.summary: Starts the Congo native victory sequence, whose later callbacks own fade cleanup and camera release.
behavior: The zero-health branch of func_0800A228_6BD4C8 schedules this entry. It clears root recovery status bit 0x1 at task +0x68, sets root +0xE8 bit 0x80 and progress flag 0x12D, emits immediate events 1 through 5, sets unsigned-halfword timer +0x8A to 120, and schedules the native victory continuation.

Later callback func_0800820C_6BB4AC creates a white screen-fade controller. Its pointer is stored at full system +0x3B018; red, green and blue are controller bytes +0x0D, +0x0E and +0x0F, and opacity is controller byte +0x10. These fields belong to a separate render object, not the root task.
Callback func_08008280_6BB520 increases fade opacity by four per update until 255, then schedules func_080082F8_6BB598. Its audio cue 0x181 is emitted only when the pre-decrement root timer is zero.
Callback func_080082F8_6BB598 decreases opacity by five per update. At zero it releases the owned fade controller through the native object-removal path before scheduling the next callback.
Only after that release does func_0800833C_6BB5DC clear root capability word +0x60, set progress flags 0x12B and 0x12E, and clear the byte at D_8015C562_15D162. The final root callback is inert.

The camera has an independent continuation: it waits for progress flag 0x12E, waits 90 updates, closes the letterbox, and releases player control. That camera chain does not release the white screen-fade controller.
cautions: A later callback address, timer or progress flag does not represent all earlier side effects. Jumping over the fade-out callback can leave a live white overlay even after the root and camera otherwise reach their final states.
Preserve the native continuation once victory begins. Re-entering the initial callback restarts its timer and emits its part events again; skipping ahead can bypass render-object cleanup.
Root task +0xDC remains its float hit-sound cooldown. It is not the fade-controller opacity or an RGBA field.
Clearing D_8015C562_15D162 or setting progress flag 0x12E does not substitute for releasing the fade controller.
Do not call this callback manually to bypass Congo damage and teardown.
